english: a debt owed, a favor one owes someone
notes: Chapter title: 大きな借り ("A Big Debt") — Gon owes Hisoka after being saved from a mad attacker; pairs with 貸し later in the chapter

english: to intercept, to meet an attack head-on
notes: text: 迎え撃つ気だ!! — I intend to meet him head-on!! (Gon decides to face Hisoka rather than flee)

english: to have the nerve to come, to dare show up (contemptuous)
notes: The やがる auxiliary adds scorn/contempt to a verb; text has the imperative form: 来やがれ!! — get over here, damn you!!

english: to catch, to bag, to claim (prey/game)
notes: Kanji specific to hunting/capturing prey (distinct from general 取る); text: 獲った!! — got it!! (claiming the plate off a defeated opponent)

english: approximately, roughly, about
notes: text: およそ7千回 — roughly 7000 times (the number of practice swings Hisoka claims to have counted)

english: intensive training, special training
notes: text: お前が特訓で竿を振り続けた回数でもある — it's also the number of times you kept swinging your rod during your special training

english: wide open, full of openings, defenseless
notes: text writes 隙 in katakana (スキ): 釣り竿を振っているお前はスキだらけだったが — you, swinging your fishing rod, were wide open, but...

english: splendid, superb, masterful
notes: text: さっきの一振りは見事だった — that last swing of yours was masterful

english: to be worthy of, to deserve
notes: text: その集中力と正確さは驚くに値する — that concentration and accuracy are worthy of astonishment

english: one's back, the rear
notes: text: 次からは自分の背後にも気をつけな — from now on, watch your own back too

english: a sign, a presence, an indication (of someone/something)
notes: text: ずっと気配を絶ってチャンスをうかがっていたのか? — had you been erasing your presence this whole time, waiting for a chance?

english: to cut off, to sever, to eliminate
notes: text: 気配を絶って — cutting off/erasing one's presence (same line as 気配)

english: to watch for, to wait for (an opportunity)
notes: text: チャンスをうかがっていたのか? — had you been watching for a chance?

english: an instant, a split second
notes: text: 誰かを攻撃する一瞬のスキを — a split-second opening to attack someone

english: one's own style, self-taught method
notes: text: 気配の消し方は自己流かい? — is your way of erasing your presence self-taught?

english: to blend into, to sneak/mix in among (something)
notes: text (causative): 自分の殺気を紛れこませました — I mixed my killing intent in among it, to hide it

english: muscle relaxation
notes: text: 吹き矢にぬられた毒は筋弛緩系だそうだ — the poison smeared on the blowdart is apparently a muscle-relaxant type

english: a blowdart, a blowgun
notes: text: 吹き矢にぬられた毒は筋弛緩系だそうだ — the poison smeared on the blowdart is apparently a muscle-relaxant type

english: to take back, to retrieve, to get back
notes: text: とり返しにきたんじゃないのか? — didn't you come to take it back?

english: to praise, to compliment
notes: text: ううんほめにきただけ — nah, I just came to praise you

english: something lent, a favor owed to you (opposite of 借り)
notes: text: それは貸しだ — consider that a loan / you owe me one; deliberately pairs with the chapter's 借り theme

english: someday, at some point, whenever
notes: text: いつか返してくれればいい — just give it back to me whenever

english: absolutely not, by no means, wanting nothing to do with (something)
notes: text: 借りなんかまっぴらだ — I want nothing to do with owing anyone a debt

english: to keep alive, to let live, to spare
notes: text (passive): 今のキミはボクに生かされている — right now, you're only alive because I'm letting you be

english: to refuse, to decline
notes: text: 断る — I refuse (a one-word declaration turning down a demand)

english: a practitioner, a skilled wielder (of a weapon/ability)
notes: text: キミがもっと殺しがいのある使い手に育つまで — until you grow into a wielder more worth killing

english: worth killing, value as a kill
notes: The -がい (甲斐) suffix means "worth of doing X" (cf. 生きがい, a reason to live); text: 殺しがいのある使い手 — a wielder worth killing

english: to slam into, to land (a blow) forcefully
notes: text: 今みたくボクの顔に一発ぶち込むことができたら — if you can land one solid punch on my face like just now

english: to entrust, to leave in someone's care, to deposit
notes: text: それまでそのプレートはキミに預ける — until then, I'll leave that plate in your care
